deepdive.sec: Digital Advertising & AI-Powered Consumer Platform Stack

bull_bear.body: INR 11B raised for strategic M&A; prioritizing acquisitions with existing advertiser relationships and tech stacks in developed markets to accelerate verticalized CPCU adoption; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on disciplined, value-driven deals with conservative valuation
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical softness in select markets; delayed M&A execution; failure to convert acquired entities to CPCU model within 2-3 years; increased competition from walled gardens in AI automation; regulatory scrutiny on first-party data and AI targeting
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, disciplined, and forward-looking; emphasized resilience of CPCU model during macro stress; highlighted IP moat in human/non-human filtration as key differentiator; M&A strategy framed as calibrated and patient, not rushed; tone is leadership-driven with strong conviction in long-term 10x vision
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Affle's 18 granted patents and 300+ enforceable claims around human vs non-human filtration are a unique, defensible moat in the GenAI era — competitors are not addressing this, making it a silent structural advantage as AI-generated fraud surges; this is not just an AI play but an anti-fraud IP play
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet as of June 30, 2026 (consolidated, INR mn): Total Assets 48,316, of which Cash & Liquid Investments 20,587 and Goodwill & Intangible Assets 15,387; Contract Assets & Trade Receivables 7,370 and Other Assets 4,972.
- Funded almost entirely by equity: Total Equity 40,576 against Total Borrowings of just 22 (INR mn), with Contract Liabilities & Trade Payables 6,123 and Other Liabilities 1,596 — i.e. a debt-free-in-substance, cash-rich structure.
- Operating Cash Flows (INR mn) charted as 2,060 / 2,603 / 2,623 / 4,260 / 5,023 for FY2022-FY2026 and 694 for Q1 FY2027; the deck notes "Operating Cashflow includes impact of FCTRs (Foreign Currency Translation Reserves) as per IND AS".
- Shareholding as on June 30, 2026: Promoters & Promoter Group 54.9%, Mutual Funds / Banks / Insurance / AIFs / QIBs 18.8%, FIIs / FCBs 17.5%, Others 8.8%, on total shares outstanding of 140,796,384 (including 173,897 held by the ESOP trust).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: India & emerging markets: 71.6% of Q4 revenue (+21.2% YoY); developed markets: 28.4% of revenue (+18.0% YoY); CPCU conversions: 120.3M at INR 60 CPCU; CTV and digital out-of-home emerging as growth vectors; fintech, e-commerce, gaming, healthcare verticals driving adoption
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Competitors relying on impression-based models and lacking direct advertiser integration | Trade Desk | loser | High | Affle's direct-to-advertiser CPCU model with first-party data integration is structurally superior to DSPs like Trade Desk that serve agencies and lack conversion-level accountability |
| Ad tech players without AI-powered human/non-human filtration | General AdTech Firms | loser | High | Affle's patent moat in distinguishing human from AI-driven engagement will become critical as agentic AI floods digital channels — competitors lack this capability |
| Global ad tech firms with weak verticalization in fintech, healthcare, and quick commerce | Affle 3i Limited | beneficiary | High | Affle's verticalized AI stack is capturing disproportionate ROI in high-LTV verticals — this is a structural advantage over horizontal platforms |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Outcome-led model: the deck states "99.8% of Revenue from Contracts with Customers contributed by CPCU model in Q1 FY2027", where advertisers are billed per converted user rather than per impression, across new-user, repeat-user and Branding/O2O conversions.
- Moat framed as tech IP and data: "Total 39 unique Patents with 18 granted and rest filed & pending across jurisdictions", "21+ years of focused R&D and innovation", an in-house Data Management Platform, and an award-winning ad-fraud platform (mFaas) addressing "privacy & ad fraud".
- Reach credential: "4 Billion+" connected devices reached, for the 12-month period July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026, with "global reach across all key regions including Asia, North America, South America, Europe and Africa".
- Accreditations cited as business credentials: "DPTM accredited" (Data Protection Trustmark certified) and "ISO 27001:2022 certified".
- Geographic straddle of emerging and developed markets: revenue split for 12M FY26 shown as "72.9% India & Emerging Markets" and "27.1% Developed Markets"; the Q1 FY2027 split is shown as 72.2% / 27.8% with Y-o-Y growth of 20.2% (India & Emerging) and 20.7% (Developed), described as "Broad-based Growth Across Markets".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Name change] The issuer is "Affle 3i Limited (Formerly known as Affle (India) Limited)"; CIN L65990DL1994PLC408172, listed as BSE scrip 542752 / NSE symbol AFFLE.
- [Internal contradiction] The deck states CPCU contributed "99.8% of Revenue from Contracts with Customers" in Q1 FY2027, while the CPCU chart shows "% Revenue Contribution" of 79% for Q1 FY2027 (and 74-76% in prior years). Both readings are reproduced as printed; the deck does not reconcile them.
- [Analyst coverage] The deck lists brokerages covering Affle across an Institutional Research Desk and an HNI/Retail Desk: Dolat Capital, Equirus Capital, Ambit Capital, Elara Capital, Amsec, DAM Capital, Anand Rathi, 360One Capital, Avendus Spark, ICICI Securities, Citi Research, ICICI Direct, Sharekhan and Ashika Equities (the split of names between the two desks is not recoverable from the extract).
- [Long-run growth framing] FY2026 headline metrics with 5-yr CAGRs as printed: Revenue INR 27,093 mn at 25.8%, EBITDA INR 6,101 mn at 30.1%, PAT INR 4,549 mn at 25.5%.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin declined from 39% to 36.5% over 7-8 quarters due to deliberate investments in premium verticalization, CTV integrations, and first-party data intelligence; data/inventory costs rose 90 bps QoQ to 63.3% of revenue; management expects margin recovery to 37-38% within 12 months as investments mature
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 20% CAGR medium-term; margin: EBITDA margin to stabilize at 22-23% after 1-year investment cycle; order inflow: not specified; capex/commissioning: no capex guidance, but INR 11B raised for M&A, not organic capex
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Global expansion in North America and Europe via M&A; monetization of CTV and digital out-of-home via CPCU model; leveraging 300+ enforceable patent claims in human/non-human filtration to capture AI-era ad spend; potential to expand into B2B SaaS for advertiser analytics
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Affle delivered 20.3% YoY revenue growth in Q4FY26 and 19.5% for FY26, driven by AI-enhanced CPCU model and verticalized integrations, with EBITDA margin expanding to 22.5% despite deliberate gross margin investments; the key change is strategic prep for M&A via INR 11B capital raise to accelerate global expansion and consolidate differentiated IP in human/non-human filtration.
